question: The set of \(x\)-values satisfying the inequality \(2\le|x-1|\le5\) is:
solution:
The quantity \(|x-1|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(1\) on the number line. The inequality requires that distance to be between \(2\) and \(5\), including both bounds.

To the left of \(1\), the permitted points run from \(1-5=-4\) to \(1-2=-1\). To the right, they run from \(1+2=3\) to \(1+5=6\).

Every permitted point lies on one of these two sides, and every point in these intervals has the required distance. Hence the complete solution is
\[
\boxed{-4\le x\le-1\quad\text{or}\quad3\le x\le6},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
